acceptance: evolve gc --only salvage --dry-run lists each salvage dir with its action (repack, drop-redundant, keep) and the bytes it frees, and changes nothing.
A non-dry run re-packs each full-history bundle against origin/main. The new bundle has the same heads, passes git bundle verify, and replaces the old one atomically.
A bundle whose heads are all reachable from origin/main is removed. A bundle whose head cannot be verified is kept and reported.
The scope never touches the salvage of a running cycle, and it writes one audit row per action.
The salvage writer creates incremental bundles, so a new salvage of one cycle costs megabytes, not a gigabyte.
Red-first tests drive the scope and the writer through the real verbs.
fix: Add the gc scope salvage: for each salvage bundle of a finished cycle, re-pack it against origin/main (heads verified one for one, git bundle verify passes, atomic replace), and remove a bundle whose heads are all reachable from origin/main. Write each action to an audit record. Make the salvage writer create incremental bundles against origin/main.
